vocabulary.example: I always wake up at seven.
I go to bed at eleven.

grammar.point: Adverbs of frequency (always / usually / sometimes / never)
grammar.explanation_en: Adverbs of frequency tell how often something happens. They usually go BEFORE the main verb, but AFTER the verb 'to be': 'I always wake up early' but 'I am always busy'.
grammar.explanation_ko: 빈도 부사는 어떤 일이 얼마나 자주 일어나는지 나타냅니다. 보통 일반동사 '앞'에 오지만, be동사 '뒤'에 옵니다: 'I always wake up early'(저는 항상 일찍 일어나요), 하지만 'I am always busy'(저는 항상 바빠요).

examples.en: She usually eats lunch at noon.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: What do you usually do on the weekend?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: I usually visit my family. I sometimes go shopping too.
dialogue.line_ko: 보통 가족을 방문해요. 가끔 쇼핑도 가요.

dialogue.speaker: A
dialogue.line: Do you always wake up early?

dialogue.speaker: B
dialogue.line: No, I never wake up early on Sundays!
dialogue.line_ko: 아니요, 일요일에는 절대 일찍 안 일어나요!

reading.title: A Typical Week
reading.text: I always wake up at six thirty on weekdays. I usually go to work by bus. On Wednesday, I have an English class in the evening. On the weekend, I never set an alarm. I sometimes meet friends on Saturday.
reading.text_ko: 저는 평일에 항상 여섯 시 반에 일어나요. 보통 버스를 타고 출근해요. 수요일 저녁에는 영어 수업이 있어요. 주말에는 절대 알람을 안 맞춰요. 토요일에는 가끔 친구를 만나요.

explanation.en: The text says 'I always wake up at six thirty on weekdays.'
The text says 'I have an English class in the evening' on Wednesday.
explanation.ko: 본문에 수요일 저녁 영어 수업이 언급됩니다.

explanation.en: The text says 'I never set an alarm' on the weekend.
explanation.ko: 본문에 'I never set an alarm.'이라고 나옵니다.
